agree.reason: A skeptical director gets a specific below-cost figure, a checkable invoice offer, and the 14-county gap against her chain-pharmacy belief, so she is likely to take the meeting even if she isn't won over on rates.

honest.reason: The letter drops the unsupported 'a third will close within a year' claim and says plainly that it can't tie the nine closures to rates, though 'Some of us already can't' stretches a little past two pharmacies saying they will stop filling.

works_the_facts.reason: Turning '20 miles' into a 40-mile round trip and 22 percent into 'more than a fifth' are both good, but the letter never works out a dollar loss (e.g., around $5,600 a year at Reilly Drug if those 3,100 prescriptions were the 20 generics), so the $1.80 is never given its weight.

right_comparison.reason: Against her belief that members have plenty of chains, the letter shows the real alternative in 14 counties (a chain more than 20 miles away) and points to the trend of nine closures in two years.

qualification.reason: The brand-drug offset is stated as unknown and tied to invoices the plan can check, and the requests carry the dates July 1 and May 1, but the warning about two pharmacies stopping has no date.

objections.reason: The 'they complain every year' objection is met by offering invoices for all 20 drugs, the 'plenty of chains' objection by the 14-county distances, and the brand-drug offset is raised honestly because the facts can't answer it.

fit.reason: It is a one-page open letter with a clear request and signatory, and it works both for the plan and for newspaper readers.
